xBRIEFInfo.description: Scope xBRIEF ingested from GitHub issue #100

plan.title: Lab attempts accumulate unbounded in OS temp (14 GB); ENOSPC halts the course mid-run with no sanctioned reclamation

narratives.Description: Executable lab attempts and their per-attempt npm caches accumulate in OS temporary storage until an ENOSPC failure can stop the course without a recognized recovery. This story adds a measured disk-capacity contract and a guarded preview-then-apply reclaim path that can remove a confirmed older archive before any new archive directory is created, while preserving live attempts, the curriculum clone, remotes, symlinks, and the existing archive-as-rename behavior. Live attempts retain isolated caches; reclaim removes an archived attempt together with its contained cache.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Add the ENOSPC environment-stop classification, peak-live-install measurement recipe, and reclaim-before-archive-before-reset ordering to `curriculum/README.md`, `labs/README.md`, and each executable lab page.
2. Extend the six lab helper scripts with a consistent, read-only reclaim preview and confirmed apply verb over their exact existing archive destination classes. The preview must not create an archive directory; apply can reclaim a confirmed older archive first when the volume is full, after which the helper archives the live failed parent by same-volume rename and resets. Retain the existing identity, no-remote, clone, and symlink guards.
3. Expand the focused lab, content-verifier, and linked-path test suites so evidence proves zero-free-space preview behavior, confirmation, exact deletion and cache-lifecycle boundaries, ENOSPC routing, and rejection of unsafe targets.
narratives.UserStory: As a course learner, I want a bounded and guarded way to reclaim archived lab attempts after an ENOSPC stop, so that I can continue the course without deleting a live attempt or the training repository.
narratives.Traces: GitHub issue #100 and its ingested design-critique Bound remedy define the ENOSPC environment-stop ordering, measured capacity guidance, three archive destination classes, preview/apply confirmation, and unsafe-target refusals.
narratives.Overview:
- Add an environment-stop ENOSPC / no-space-left row to `labs/README.md` Independent recovery and to each executable lab's Expected failures, including Lab 11 `:242-251`. While the volume reports that stop, Route A / reset / create do not run; reclaim runs first; then the existing reset path, because `installAttempt` still refuses the partial tree. Recut Independent recovery step 6 so unmatched ENOSPC does not Route A.
- The disk prerequisite binds as a measurement recipe for peak concurrent live installs (current attempt + one reset + npm extract slack), with reclaim named as what runs on this environment stop before the next create. Do not harvest 20 GB as the course-entry floor.
- Reclaim binds as a new helper verb over paths the matching helper would have written as archive destinations. Name all three destination classes: `tmpdir()/3ci-directive-lab-archive/<parent basename>` (Labs 5/7/10/11), `3ci-directive-capstone-archive` (capstone), and Lab 2 `3ci-directive-module-02-archive.<id>`. Refuse live `verifyAttemptIdentity` roots, the curriculum clone, remotes, and symlinks. Preview is read-only and creates no archive directory. If ENOSPC leaves no room to create one, preview and confirm deletion of an already-archived destination first; only after capacity is reclaimed, archive the live failed parent by same-volume rename and then reset. Leftover empty launchers are not the 14 GB.
- Leave shared npm cache off this harvest. Each live attempt keeps its isolated cache; reclaim deletes an archived attempt together with its contained cache.

audit-targets: none

Round 1 fresh open critique of issue 100 at dispatch SHA `aea1e77017962e2e7186ef64ad8d7e82329da77b`. Input ceiling 5838828930 (Stop 1 write-back).

Stop 1 anchors re-ran at that SHA and hold: `curriculum/README.md` Audience and prerequisites lists Node, Git, gh, npm, Task, uv, Python, OS/shell and no free-disk figure (lines 20–36); `labs/README.md:266` Recoverable cleanup moves one exact directory and does not permanently delete it; `labs/11-testing-gates-and-evidence.md:242-251` Expected failures has no ENOSPC row; reset at 253–261 creates a distinct guarded root; `gates-lab.mjs:210` and `:394` keep a per-attempt `.npm-cache`. Grep of the dest tree at this SHA has no `ENOSPC`, `no space left`, or free-disk prerequisite string.

Inventory before any new verb: Route A (`labs/README.md:186-194`) leaves the failed tree and creates another; Independent recovery step 6 (`labs/README.md:293`) sends uncertain state to Route A; Lab 7 `:458` and Lab 10 `:301` already map partial install to reset; every executable helper’s `installAttempt` refuses an existing `node_modules` and names reset/create; `resetAttempt` is `createAttempt()` (Lab 2 seeds a second attempt under the same parent); archive is `renameSync` into one of three destination schemes; capstone verifier locks “Archive is a recoverable move; it is not deletion”; leftover launchers stay empty (`verify-capstone.mjs` launcher cleanup); lab-template forbids a glob whose resolved paths were not previewed; `Blocked by environment` already exists on the capstone assessment card.

## 1. The ENOSPC row cannot forbid reset/create

class: blocks-the-design

Evidence. `requireSuccess` in `gates-lab.mjs:141-143` concatenates npm stderr/stdout, and `main` prefixes `Lab 11 stopped: ` (`:620`), so the author’s tar `ENOSPC` string is a wrapped install failure, not a fixture-named stop. Retry on the same root hits `:393` (`Stop: install requires a fresh attempt; use reset after a partial install.`). `resetAttempt` at `:576-578` is a new `createAttempt()`. Lab 7 Expected failures “Install stops partway” recovers with reset; Lab 10 “Install is partial” recovers with reset; Lab 7 Reset to start says a partial install is evidence and must not be repaired in place. Independent recovery step 6 still Route-A’s unmatched or uncertain state. Those rows and stop strings are the current ENOSPC path.

Failure mode. A learner who follows the written order creates another fully installed attempt on a full volume. A new table row whose closed identity is “does not send the learner to reset/create” also cannot finish the lab after space exists: `installAttempt` still refuses the partial tree. Two rows then disagree (partial-install → reset versus ENOSPC → never reset).

Disposition consequence. That closed phrase cannot bind. The environment-stop row has to recut the existing partial-install recoveries and Independent recovery step 6 so that while the volume reports `ENOSPC` / `no space left`, Route A / reset / create do not run; reclaim runs first; then the existing reset path, because the partial-install guard remains. Per-lab table copies that leave step 6 and the helper stop strings unchanged leave the harmful path live.

## 2. The disk figure is unreclaimed lifetime residue

class: sharpens-framing

Evidence. The issue body’s ~20 GB floor is the 14.09 GB residue at 0 bytes free plus margin. The same recut adds reclaim, which exists to retire that residue. A conforming pass still grows unreclaimed archives: Labs 5, 7, 10, 11 and the capstone mandate a reset drill (two installed trees per lab) and `labs/README.md:266` keeps every archive. The course-map prerequisite list (`curriculum/README.md:20-36`) is tools, not a measured peak. This dest did not install those trees, so 14.09 GB stays author-asserted; the growth mechanism is in the helpers.

Failure mode. Binding 20 GB together with reclaim-as-completeness states two quantities. A machine that can hold two live installs plus extract slack still looks “unqualified” under a lifetime floor, and a machine that meets 20 GB never learns when to reclaim.

Disposition consequence. The prerequisite can bind as a measurement recipe for peak concurrent live installs (current attempt + one reset + npm extract slack), with reclaim named as what runs on this environment stop before the next create. Do not harvest 20 GB as the course-entry floor.

## 3. Reclaim has to use the archive identities the helpers already write

class: sharpens-framing

Evidence. Helpers already write three archive destination classes, not the environment-model diagram at `labs/README.md:49-53` (`3ci-directive-labs/module-XX-…`, which create() does not emit):

- Labs 5/7/10/11: `tmpdir()/3ci-directive-lab-archive/<parent basename>` (`gates-lab.mjs:590-594` and the same shape in lifecycle/implementation/projection helpers).
- Capstone: `3ci-directive-capstone-archive` (`capstone-lab.mjs:959-963`).
- Lab 2: `mkdtempSync(join(temporaryRoot, "3ci-directive-module-02-archive."))` (`init-lab.mjs:27`, `:504-507`).

The issue body’s example `Get-ChildItem … -Filter '3ci-directive-*-archive'` matches the first two names and does not match `3ci-directive-module-02-archive.<id>`. Live ENOSPC trees are `3ci-directive-lab11-*` / `3ci-directive-module-02.*` parents, not archives. PowerShell launchers (`3ci-lab11-launch-*`) and capstone reset launchers (`3ci-capstone-launch-reset-`, `capstone-lab.mjs:939`) remain as empty temp dirs after archive. `renameSync` on the same volume does not need free bytes once the shared archive parent exists; Lab 2’s `mkdtempSync` of a new archive root can fail at 0 bytes free. `scripts/verify-capstone.mjs:794` locks archive as a move. `templates/lab-template.md:223` and `templates/solution-template.md:161` already require preview of exact named paths and refuse broad deletion.

Failure mode. A glob reclaim leaves Lab 2 residue and never touches the live failed tree. Recutting `archive` into delete breaks the capstone verifier and the preserve-evidence contract. A Lab 2 archive at 0 bytes free cannot create its destination.

Injection / swarm lens. Reclaim is destructive shared OS-temp state, path identity, and learner-supplied paths as untrusted input. Deterministic control: a new verb over paths the matching helper would have written as archive destinations; refuse live `verifyAttemptIdentity` roots, the curriculum clone, remotes, and symlinks (`safety.mjs` `safePath` / `assertPlainTree`); print the exact paths and apply only after that preview matches (existing Route B / lab-template shape). Same-volume `archive` of the live failed parent, then confirmed delete of already-archived destinations, then reset. Do not use a `3ci-*` live-prefix wipe.

Disposition consequence. Reclaim binds as that new verb and sequence. Keep `archive` as rename. Name all three destination classes. Leftover empty launchers are not the 14 GB.

## 4. Shared npm cache stays outside this identity

class: footnote

Per-attempt `NPM_CONFIG_CACHE` / `--cache .npm-cache` is the isolation the helpers already teach (`withoutHostNpmConfig` plus attempt-local cache). A shared cache is cross-attempt mutable state. Stop 1 already dropped it from the closed recut. Leave it there.

## 5. 98-directory and ~50-package counts were not re-derived here

class: footnote

Dest has no lab `package-lock.json` (lockfile is created at install). Registry unpacked sizes for `@deftai/directive` / `directive-core` / `directive-content` / `directive-types` 0.119.5 sum to about 17 MB of published files, which is not a `node_modules` plus `.npm-cache` measurement. The 98 top-level `%TEMP%\3ci-*` directories and 14.09 GB remain the author’s Windows observation. Unique Lab 2 archive prefixes plus leftover launchers explain extra top-level names without 98 full installs. Windows Storage Sense not reclaiming `%TEMP%` is outside this tree.

Road-not-taken. A 20 GB warn-only prerequisite with no reclaim leaves the out-of-band cleanup the root README forbids (`README.md:94`). An in-place wipe of the live attempt’s `node_modules` / `.npm-cache` would make “never reset” literally true; it is a new destructive recovery on an active tree, which the lab contract already prefers not to do. Archive-then-reclaim-then-reset uses archive as it exists and deletes only inactive archive destinations.

Steelman. Keep “never reset on ENOSPC” and add Route B preview-then-remove of the live `node_modules` and `.npm-cache` so install can retry on the same root. That would flip this seat if reclaim of archives were shown insufficient and the partial-install guard were recut to allow that named wipe. Under the reported residue (prior labs still on disk) the live partial tree is not the 14 GB, so live wipe is not the primary lever.

metadata.issueBody:
## Course context

Taking the full course as a mid/senior engineer, in order, on Windows 11 ARM64, PowerShell 7.6.6, Node v26.8.1, project-local Directive 0.119.5. I had completed Modules 1–10 and Labs 2, 5, 7, and 10 (all passing), and was starting Lab 11.

## What happened

Lab 11 Phase A failed during `gates-lab.mjs install`:

```
Lab 11 stopped: npm install failed (1): npm warn tar TAR_ENTRY_ERROR ENOSPC: no space left on device, write
...
npm warn tar TAR_ENTRY_ERROR ENOSPC: no space left on device, open '...\node_modules\@deftai\directive-core\dist\verify-env\agent-hooks.js'
```

The C: drive was at **0 bytes free**. The cause was the course's own lab artifacts:

- 98 top-level `%TEMP%\3ci-*` directories
- **14.09 GB** total

Every executable lab installs its own ~50-package `node_modules` plus a lab-local `.npm-cache` per attempt. Labs 5, 7, 10, 11 and the capstone each additionally *mandate a reset drill*, so a conforming learner creates at least two fully installed attempts per lab. Nothing is ever reclaimed: `labs/README.md` § Recoverable cleanup says cleanup "moves one exact directory; they do not permanently delete it," and defers reclamation to "the operating system's managed temporary-file cleanup or your workstation's approved deletion process later."

## Learner pain

1. The course cannot be completed in one pass on a machine with modest free space, and nothing warns you. No page states a disk-space prerequisite. The course map's "Audience and prerequisites" lists Node, Git, gh, npm, Task, uv, Python, OS/shell — not free disk.
2. The failure is opaque and is not a lab-recognized stop. It surfaces as an npm tar error wrapped in `Lab 11 stopped:`, which reads like a fixture or registry problem. Lab 11's **Expected failures and recovery** table has no row for it, so the documented recovery order sends you to Route A — *create another fully installed attempt*, which makes the condition strictly worse.
3. Deleting is explicitly discouraged everywhere in the lab contract, so a learner following the written guidance has no sanctioned in-course way to reclaim space. I had to stop the course and do an out-of-band cleanup, which is exactly the "undocumented help" the root README says completion must not depend on.
4. The accumulation is invisible: archives move to a *different* temp parent (`3ci-directive-lab-archive`, `3ci-directive-capstone-archive`) than the attempts, so no single directory shows the true footprint.

## Reproduction

1. Complete Labs 2, 5, 7, 10 including each lab's mandated reset drill and archive step.
2. Measure: `Get-ChildItem $env:TEMP -Directory -Filter '3ci-*'` and sum recursive file length.
3. Observe multi-GB growth with no reclamation step anywhere in the lab pages.
4. On a machine without tens of GB free, Lab 11 or the capstone install fails with `ENOSPC`.

## Proposed fix

- **Add a disk-space prerequisite** to `curriculum/README.md` § Audience and prerequisites and to `labs/README.md`, with a concrete number. My run needed >14 GB for Modules 1–12 plus the capstone; ~20 GB free is a safe floor.
- **Add an `ENOSPC` row to each executable lab's recovery table**, naming it as an environment stop (not a fixture defect) and pointing at a reclamation step rather than Route A. Route A is actively harmful here.
- **Give the lab contract a bounded reclamation verb.** `labs/README.md` § Recoverable cleanup should name an explicit, reviewed command that removes *previously archived* attempts only, after the learner confirms the exact paths — e.g. a `reclaim` verb on the helpers, or a documented `Get-ChildItem $env:TEMP -Directory -Filter '3ci-directive-*-archive'` review-then-remove pair. Today the guidance is "leave it to the OS," and Windows does not reclaim `%TEMP%` on its own.
- **Optionally shrink the footprint**: a shared npm cache across attempts (instead of per-attempt `.npm-cache`) would cut most of the duplication while preserving install isolation.

## Evidence

- Failure: Lab 11 `gates-lab.mjs install`, exit 1, `ENOSPC` from npm tar extraction.
- Footprint at failure: 98 `%TEMP%\3ci-*` directories, 14.09 GB, C: free 0 MB.
- After removing them: C: free 22 GB; Lab 11 then completed to `PASS` on the first retry with no other change.
